model: 0.5 flying fish / 0.5 zebrafish morphological blend (two-parent test case)
units_and_axes: glTF Y-up; head at +X, back at +Y, the fish's left side at -Z. The adult / resolved set has SL = 0.82 model units; earlier growth stages are built at their TRUE relative size SL(age)/SL(adult), so development plays as real growth. standard_length_m = 0.1209 m sets the metres per model unit.
MORPHOLOGICAL_NOT_GENETIC: MORPHOLOGICAL interpolation, not genetic hybridisation. Averaging two species' body parameters says nothing about whether such an animal could be bred, is viable, or is developmentally reachable; genomes do not average. Flying fish and zebrafish are not crossable. This is a shape, not an organism.
generative_model: parameters = SUM over parents ( weight_i * parent_i.parameter ) + delta

lean_recheck.why: a design inherits whatever constraints its parents satisfy; every delta needs re-checking

standard_length_m.drives: real-world standard length; sets the metres-per-model-unit scale

body_mass_kg.drives: wet mass; with flight_muscle_fraction sets the girdle muscle volume

body_depth_over_SL.drives: maximum body depth / SL (full depth, not half)

body_section_exponent.drives: superellipse exponent of the trunk cross-section (2 = ellipse)

head_fraction_SL.drives: fraction of SL over which the snout rounds off

peduncle_depth_frac.drives: caudal peduncle depth / maximum body depth

peduncle_width_frac.drives: caudal peduncle width / maximum body width

pectoral_len_over_SL.drives: longest pectoral fin ray, base to tip, / SL

pectoral_span_over_SL.drives: pectoral tip-to-tip span / SL (both fins, across the body)

pectoral_area_over_SL2.drives: membrane area of BOTH pectoral fins / SL^2 (the Park & Choi / physics-flier convention)

pectoral_ray_count.drives: lepidotrichia per pectoral fin (one named mesh each)

flight_muscle_fraction.drives: pectoral/girdle muscle mass / body mass; sets the VOLUME of pectoral_muscle_L/R, so it visibly thickens the girdle musculature

mesh_detail.drives: global mesh resolution multiplier (1.0 = the committed flying-fish detail)

derived_from_the_mesh.flight_muscle_note: the pectoral girdle musculature is sized by VOLUME from flight_muscle_fraction x body_mass, then clipped to what fits inside the skin. fit_fraction < 1 means the requested muscle mass does not fit in this body at this schematic geometry.
derived_from_the_mesh.measured_how: areas are membrane surface areas measured on the exported mesh; span is the tip-to-tip extent of the pectoral fins in the spanwise axis. The physical values use standard_length_m / 0.8200 model units.

definitions.pectoral_aspect_ratio: pectoral_span^2 / (area of ONE pectoral fin), the Park & Choi 2010 convention
definitions.lifting_area_m2: pectoral (both) + pelvic (both) + caudal membrane area, the physics/flier convention
definitions.flight_muscle_volume_m3: flight_muscle_fraction * body_mass / 1060 kg/m3 (teleost muscle density, assumed)

parameter_vs_mesh_check.what: the parameters ask for a span and an area; these are what the exported MESH actually has
parameter_vs_mesh_check.verdict: NO FIT was applied: the pectoral geometry is driven by pectoral_len_over_SL (this is what keeps the reference faithful to the committed flying-fish.glb). The span and area parameters are therefore TARGETS THAT THE MESH DOES NOT MEET, and the ratios above say by how much. For the flying fish this exposes a real discrepancy: the committed mesh's pectoral membrane is much broader (lower aspect ratio) than the Park & Choi 2010 specimen it is compared with. Note the measured value is a projected planform area while the mesh value is membrane surface area, which accounts for a few per cent, not for a factor of two.

morph_targets.label: flying fish with enlarged pectoral fins (Exocoetidae), generic

morph_target_rule: set the weights of the two bracketing targets to (1-f, f) and every other target to 0; weights always sum to 1. See anatomy-model/parametric/INTEGRATION.md.

inside_check.what: superellipse norm of every internal piece against the skin surface; <= the piece's limit means it does not poke outside

layers: outer (skin, eyes, fin membranes) / muscle / skeleton / organ
